html:
The Saura were a Siouan-speaking people of the upper Dan River in the Piedmont of North Carolina and Virginia. Archaeologists have dug their villages at Upper and Lower Saura Town, in today's Stokes and Rockingham counties. Most historians identify them with the Cheraw.

Spanish expeditions of Hernando de Soto in 1540 and Juan Pardo in the 1560s probably met their ancestors farther south, under the name Xualla. In the early 1700s, under raids from the north and the pressure of English traders, the Saura moved south to the Pee Dee River in South Carolina. After the Yamasee War they joined the Catawba. Neighbours: Keyauwee and Occaneechi.
